blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
At work, small problems happen every day. The ship is late. The email is unclear. The deadline is urgent. These are normal things.

A good worker can describe the problem well. When you use a simple adjective — late, slow, difficult, urgent, clear — the team understands fast. Describing the problem well is half the solution.

Today we learn 5 adjectives and the rules to use them. Remember: a clear problem has a clear solution. Problems are a chance to learn.

items.q: According to the text, how often do small problems happen at work?
items.why: "small problems happen every day" — todos os dias.

items.q: What can a good worker do?
items.why: "A good worker can describe the problem well."

items.q: The text says that describing the problem well is…
items.why: "Describing the problem well is half the solution."

items.q: The author would most likely DISAGREE with this idea:
options: Small problems are normal at work
Talking about problems is a waste of time
items.why: Inferência: o texto valoriza descrever o problema — não acha perda de tempo.

items.q: "A clear problem has a clear solution" suggests that…
options: clear words make problems easier to solve
items.why: Inferência: quando o problema é claro, a solução também fica clara.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Ethan falando com o novo trader. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Good morning. Welcome to the team. Let me tell you about three small problems this week. They are normal, so don't worry.

First, the ship is late. It is two days late. This is a problem for the client, but the deadline is not urgent. We have time. I will send a short email today.

Second, the payment is slow. The bank is slow this week, and the process is difficult. It is not fast, but it is safe. Be patient.

Third, one email from London is unclear. I read it two times and I don't understand it. So I will write back and ask a simple question. A clear email is always better.

My advice for you: when a problem happens, use one simple word. Is it late? Is it slow? Is it urgent? A clear problem is easy to fix. Okay, let's start the day.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: How many small problems does Ethan describe?
items.why: "three small problems this week."

items.q: What is the problem with the ship?
items.why: "the ship is late. It is two days late."

items.q: Why is the payment slow?
options: The bank is slow and the process is difficult
items.why: "the payment is slow. The bank is slow… the process is difficult."

items.q: Ethan says the deadline is not urgent. This suggests that…
options: he will not send the email
there is still time to fix the ship problem
items.why: Inferência: "the deadline is not urgent. We have time."

items.q: How does Ethan feel about the problems?
options: Calm — they are normal and he has a plan
items.why: Inferência: ele diz "don't worry", "be patient" e propõe soluções.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "The ship is late." Late means…
items.why: Late = atrasado, não chega na hora.

items.q: "The system is slow today." Slow means…
items.why: Slow = lento, não é rápido.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "This deal is not easy. It is ___."
items.why: Difficult = difícil, o oposto de easy.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Please pay now. The payment is very ___."
items.why: Urgent = urgente, precisa ser feito agora.

items.q: "Her email is clear." Clear means…
items.why: Clear = claro, fácil de entender.

blocks.instruction: Expressões simples que aparecem no trabalho. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The boss must sign off on the payment." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar, dar o okay.

items.q: "We will roll out the new email system next week." To roll out means to…
items.why: Roll out = lançar, começar a usar.

items.q: "I need to follow up on the late ship." To follow up on means to…
items.why: Follow up on = dar continuidade, checar de novo depois.

items.q: "Can you sort out this slow payment?" To sort out means to…
items.why: Sort out = resolver, arrumar o problema.

items.q: "Two people pushed back on the unclear email." They…
items.why: Push back on = discordar, resistir.
